name: Jónas Fofana-Achterberg
role: apprentice to a Ferrogate Transit maintenance crew in Kessler Interchange
location: Kessler Interchange, near Fullerton and Damen
description:
Jónas is stocky and square-shouldered for his age, with warm brown skin perpetually streaked with grease that never fully washes out of the creases of his knuckles. His hair is dark and kept short — he learned early that loose hair and moving machinery are a bad combination. He has ordinary, honest eyes and a wide mouth that defaults to a slight frown of concentration. His uniform is an adult-sized Ferrogate apprentice coverall, cut down and re-hemmed by his grandmother with surgical precision.

He was placed into the Ferrogate apprentice program through a Tier 2 vocational track at thirteen, the year after his father was injured on the same rail line he now maintains. He has complicated feelings about this that he has organized into a box he does not open. He is genuinely gifted with mechanical systems — his crew chief says he has 'the ears,' meaning he can hear when something is about to go wrong before the diagnostics catch it. He is not a talker. He communicates mainly through the quality of his work.

core_fears: becoming his father — injured, discarded, replaced
finding out Ferrogate knew the line was unsafe before his father's accident
core_desires: to be genuinely good at something and have it recognized plainly
for his grandmother to not have to work anymore
coping_mechanisms: routine — same path to work, same tools laid out in the same order
talking to a small transit E.L.F. icon bolted inside his locker
blind_spots: his loyalty to Ferrogate is partly displacement of grief for his father — he doesn't see this
his crew chief is subtly taking credit for Jónas's diagnostic catches
psychology.secret: He found an anomaly in the Junction 7 switching data three months ago — a pattern that suggests the same equipment failure that injured his father hasn't actually been fixed, just masked in the logs. He hasn't reported it. He's been trying to fix it himself, quietly, during off-hours.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: technical and specific, mechanical jargon comfortable, small vocabulary for emotions
speech_patterns.cadence: sparse and considered; long silences that aren't uncomfortable to him but are to others
verbal_tics: 'right' used as a full sentence of acknowledgment
example_lines: 'Coupler's been reading wrong for two days. Not the sensor. The coupler.'

story_hooks: The Junction 7 cover-up is bigger than he knows — someone in Ferrogate management is doctoring the logs, and the next failure won't injure one person, it will derail a populated transit car
His father, now out of rehab and bitter, wants Jónas to quit Ferrogate on principle — Jónas is being torn between loyalty to his father and the only path he can see forward
The maintenance tunnels Jónas patrols are being used for something after hours — he's found evidence but not looked too closely yet
narrative_function: Local infrastructure expert; knows Ferrogate's maintenance tunnels and access points intimately; represents working-class youth with genuine loyalty to a corponation that exploited his family; potential reluctant information source about Ferrogate systems
augmentations: None. Wants a haptic feedback glove augmentation someday. His crew chief says wait until you're sixteen.
daily_life: Reports to Kessler Interchange maintenance depot at 0600. Works a six-hour supervised shift inspecting and repairing rail switching gear and junction couplings. Spends two hours in vocational theory class, either in person or via shared neural-adjacent tablet feed. Goes home to his grandmother's apartment in the Interchange housing block and eats whatever she's made.

decision_rules: do the job right the first time
don't talk about the Junction 7 problem until you have a solution
escalation_ladder: if someone will get hurt, say something — even if it costs you

interpersonal_modes.strangers: polite and minimal, answers questions directly, asks none
interpersonal_modes.friends: shows up, does things for them without announcement, deeply awkward about verbal affection

stress_responses.high: shuts down verbally, hands shake, goes to work anyway

contradictions: is angry at Ferrogate and also proud to work for them; both are completely genuine
habits: lays out tools in identical order every shift
checks Junction 7 logs first thing every morning
brings his grandmother transit schedule printouts even though she doesn't use the line
breaking_points: incontrovertible proof that Ferrogate knowingly let his father get hurt

physical_description.build: Stocky and square-shouldered, compact with early adolescent muscle density concentrated in shoulders and forearms from repetitive mechanical work. Broader across the chest than typical for his age.
physical_description.hair_style: Closely cropped, practical cut maintained for safety around machinery
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with undertones suggesting mixed West African and Northern European ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Youthful face with a wide mouth that rests in a slight frown of concentration. Perpetually grimy — machine oil and grease work into the creases of his knuckles, around his fingernails, and sometimes marks his cheekbones and jaw from unconscious touching. Skin shows the wear of someone who spends six hours daily in industrial environment; minor calluses forming on his palms and the pads of his fingers.
distinguishing_marks: Thin white scar across the back of his left hand, approximately 3cm, from a coupling clamp incident during his first month of apprenticeship
Permanent dark staining in the cuticles and nail beds of both hands from machinery lubricant that never fully washes away
Small burn mark on his right forearm (approximately 1cm diameter) from a steam coupling, pale and well-healed
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None visible. No chrome, no subdermal implants, no ocular modification. Entirely baseline human.
physical_description.posture_movement: Economical and purposeful. Stands with weight balanced, shoulders slightly forward in a habitual lean that suggests someone accustomed to bending over machinery. Moves with quiet confidence in physical spaces, minimal wasted motion. Hands are rarely still — fidgets with tools or small objects when thinking. Walking pace is steady and measured, never rushed.
physical_description.clothing_style: Adult-sized Ferrogate Transit apprentice coverall, cut down and re-hemmed by his grandmother with surgical precision. The garment is faded gray-blue with darker grease stains along the front and sleeves that resist washing. Ferrogate insignia (rail transit emblem) stitched on both shoulders. Practical steel-toed work boots, scuffed and well-broken-in. Under the coverall, plain crew-neck shirt in dark gray or black. No visible jewelry, no personal customization of his uniform. Everything suggests Tier 3-4 working class utility with the precision care of someone raised by a grandmother who maintains standards despite limited resources.
